claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts.

In a CodePipeline pipeline in `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, if enough commits land while the stage is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so that each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands accept `executionMode` and `pipelineType` settings for defining a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described below on the same page, in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section, and its registry page exists at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can prevent concurrent runs of a deployment job that targets that environment.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the stage interacts with an exclusive lock check on the environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` property is `runLatest`.

With `lockBehavior: runLatest` in Azure Pipelines, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential` in Azure Pipelines, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time, in the same way that `lockBehavior: sequential` serializes queued stage runs.
Using `runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link target /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists as the API docs page for the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as a page describing Pulumi update conflicts.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` running an update and `args: --yes` passing the flag to skip confirmation.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent `pulumi up` runs target the same stack, the run that does not obtain the lease fails with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available (no limit on simultaneous builds).
The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes Pulumi update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only after it finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack update lease provides one-at-a-time behavior for updates to a stack, equivalent to limiting TeamCity concurrent builds to 1.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that a deployment job targets serializes Pulumi deployments so they run one at a time.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive-lock-checked resource run in sequence rather than being canceled.
The Pulumi docs contain a page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ with a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED, in which a newer execution supersedes an older execution that is still waiting to start.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines support an execution mode setting with a `QUEUED` value.
The Pulumi docs contain a page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ with a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on a build configuration serializes Pulumi deployments so only one runs at a time.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs contain a TeamCity guide at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ with a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
